chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Rehearsing Jimmie Lunceford and arranging for his Cotton Club show with Lena Horne
summary: Whaley rehearsed Lunceford at the Lafayette, called it the greatest band, and arranged two numbers for him at the Cotton Club for $150, with Lena Horne and Avon Long.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: After they played Philadelphia and came back, their pay jumped --and Duke was at the Cotton Club, and I used to go up there all the time hanging around, listening, and I was rehearsing shows all the time, then, see, and Jimmy Lunceford's show band came in and I rehearsed them, and when I got through rehearsing, I went out in the street and told the guy, man, this was the greatest band in the world. Ah!
And they had a boy playing trumpet and he could hit those high notes and the big number was 'Tiger Rag,' and they
had Willie Smith in there, and they had Louis -- a fellow named Louis on the trumpet, also. But I say that's the greatest band in the world.

So when Jimmy went to the Cotton Club right after Duke left, my man asked him if he had gotten anybody to arrange, so he said there was a boy downtown there at the Lafayette, and they called me up and I went up there and I arranged two numbers -- Here Goes a Fool in Love, and I'm Going To Love You as Long as I Live.
Lena Horne was the ingenue, and what's the boy -- oh, what's his name? Gates or Yates or something. He was in Brown Sugar.
The boy who was in Brown Sugar.
Avon Long. Avon Long! He was a singer and Lena was a pretty girl -- she didn't sing then when
I first met her at the Cotton Club. But Avon used to sing that number.

Yes, Lena Horne. Sing it to Lena Horne, 'I'm gonna love you as long as I love, da, da, da ... yep. Then they had another band number, you know, all the men. 'Here Goes a Fool In Love.' I arranged those two numbers, I charged the man $150, and I had to go up every -- you know, every time trying to get the money. He'd pay me a little, a fellow named Red used to be -- hey, what you want, kid? I said, 'I want my money' and finally I got it all.
It's funny how we have to struggle for our money in show business.
Yeah. And see, Ethel Waters was one of my big stars, that you know, came under me -- Lena Horne.
Ethel? I met her at the Lafayette Theatre. And as I said, Josephine Baker -- Josephine -- was that her name?
